newsitem.title: RUSSIA: WEIGHTLIFTING-POWER STRUGGLE ROCKS RUSSIAN RULING BODY.
newsitem.headline: WEIGHTLIFTING-POWER STRUGGLE ROCKS RUSSIAN RULING BODY.

text.p: Russian weightlifting has been thrown into confusion by the sacking of a top official over financial irregularities and a court order that the governing body reinstate ousted Soviet-era boss Viktor Polyakov.
Vladimir Maslyayev said on Monday he had been appointed general secretary of the Russian Weightlifting Federation after Yuri Sandalov was removed last month "for serious financial violations".

He denied that Polyakov, who presided for a quarter of a century over the world-beating Soviet weightlifting team, had returned as federation president following a court ruling last week that his 1994 sacking had been illegal.

"Polyakov has nothing to do with this post any more," Maslyayev said by telephone from the federation's Moscow headquarters. He said Israil Arsamakov, elected president in 1994, had been re-elected in December and remained in the job.
But Polyakov, contacted at home, said: "I am the president of the Russian Weightlifting Federation."
Maslyayev gave no details of the allegations against Sandalov, who was appointed general secretary in 1994.
The row was reminiscent of many which have broken out in Russian sports following the collapse of the state-funded sporting machine along with the rest of the Soviet superpower.
Russia remains a major force in world weightlifting but its domination is threatened by advances from China, Turkey and Greece, as well as the other former Soviet states.
